rows.title: In Alabama, Workers At Amazon Warehouse Are Poised For Union Vote
rows.standfirst: Some 5,800 workers at the Bessemer facility will vote starting this week on joining the Retail, Wholesale and Department Store Union, potentially making it Amazon's first union shop in the U.S.

rows.title: 2 Prominent 'New York Times' Journalists Depart Over Past Behavior
rows.standfirst: Science reporter Don McNeil Jr. admitted he was wrong to have used a racial slur. Producer Andy Mills said he had learned from past misbehavior but a "pressure campaign" made it impossible to stay.

rows.title: Fox News Media Cancels 'Lou Dobbs Tonight'
rows.standfirst: The 5 p.m. show will be replaced by Fox Business Tonight starting Monday.

rows.title: Kroger Offers $100 Bonus To Employees Who Get Vaccinated
rows.standfirst: Businesses across the country are encouraging employees to receive a coronavirus vaccine. Kroger Co. employees will receive a $100 bonus once they have been fully vaccinated.

rows.title: Jobs Friday: Extremely Not Good
rows.standfirst: The US economy created 49,000 jobs last month, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. That's a lot less that people had hoped and shows that the recovery has slowed.

rows.title: Biden Doesn't Think $15 Minimum Wage Hike Will Survive COVID-19 Relief Bill
rows.standfirst: President Biden has called to more than double the federal minimum wage as part of his economic relief plan.

rows.title: The Lasting Power Of Whitney Houston's National Anthem
rows.standfirst: Why does Whitney Houston's 1991 Super Bowl national anthem still resonate 30 years later? Sam chats with author and Black Girl Songbook host Danyel Smith about that moment of Black history and what it says about race, patriotism and pop culture.

rows.title: Live Performance, The Pandemic And The Domino Effect Of Dark Stages
rows.standfirst: The pandemic leveled live performance, and the industry is last in line for a return to normal.

rows.title: Fine and Punishment
rows.standfirst: When you get out of prison, you have to start paying off fees. Some are related to committing a crime. Others are not. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Myanmar's Coup Will Be 'Painful' For Already Struggling Economy, Analysts Warn
rows.standfirst: Myanmar's economy is already suffering due to COVID-19. Analysts say an imposition of broad economic sanctions in response to the coup could harm the country and result in greater Chinese influence.

rows.title: Senate Says No To $15 Minimum Wage For Now, But Democrats Vow To Push On
rows.standfirst: Raising the federal minimum wage to $15 remains a priority of President Biden and Democrats after the Senate approved an amendment prohibiting a wage increase during the pandemic.

rows.title: U.S. Adds Just 49,000 Jobs In January, 'Not Anywhere Close' To Recovering Those Lost
rows.standfirst: U.S. employers added 49,000 jobs last month, after a pandemic-driven slump in December. Unemployment fell to 6.3%.

rows.title: GameStop Mania Likely Won't Happen Again. Here's How To Invest Wisely
rows.standfirst: Some investors in a Reddit group made a pile of money off GameStop's wild ride. But it's unlikely something similar will happen again. Here's how you can make smart investments.

rows.title: Suppliers Field Growing Demand For Seeds From Pandemic Gardeners
rows.standfirst: Many people stuck at home during the pandemic turned to gardening for the first time. The unexpected spike in demand has seed suppliers struggling to keep up.

rows.title: Johnson & Johnson Applies For Emergency Use Authorization For COVID-19 Vaccine
rows.standfirst: The company's vaccine has shown to be 85% effective against severe forms of the disease. Patients will only need to receive one shot instead of two, as with other vaccines already in use in the U.S.

rows.title: There's A Good Chance Your Valentine's Flowers Come From Colombia
rows.standfirst: The country is the top flower exporter to the U.S. When the pandemic hit, farmers feared they'd have to destroy flower beds and lay off thousands of workers. Here's why that didn't happen.

rows.title: Days Of COVID And Roses
rows.standfirst: The Covid-19 lockdown sent the flower market into free fall, but recently, flower prices have been picking up again. Who are the culprits behind this? Our old friends supply and demand, of course!

rows.title: We Buy A Superhero 1: Origins
rows.standfirst: Marvel has 7,000 characters, many of them forgotten. We want to buy one from their vault and launch our own little Planet Money franchise. | Find the full Planet Money Superhero series here.

rows.title: The Union Fight At Amazon, Plus 'Your Korean Dad'
rows.standfirst: An Amazon fulfillment center in Bessemer, Alabama, has become ground zero in a battle that could change Amazon as we know it. Sam chats with a worker about his experience, and labor reporter and organizer Kim Kelly talks about what the fight for unionization in Amazon's warehouses means for the future of workers' rights. Plus, Sam talks to Nick Cho, known as Your Korean Dad on TikTok, about becoming the internet's favorite dad.

rows.title: Renters Are Getting Evicted Despite CDC Order — 'I'm Scared'
rows.standfirst: Some landlords are evicting tenants despite an order from the CDC aimed at stemming the spread of COVID-19 by preventing evictions. That has led to calls to strengthen protections.

rows.title: The Pen Is Mightier Than The Suit
rows.standfirst: The Hollywood Writers Guild just declared victory in their fight with talent agencies. Who do they have to thank for their historic win? Among other factors, possibly ... the pandemic?

rows.title: Trump Official Cited Security To Kill Visas For VOA Staffers. Emails Say Otherwise
rows.standfirst: Under Trump, the agency over the Voice of America stopped granting requests for visa extensions for foreign journalists to reserve jobs for Americans. The agency had cited security concerns.

rows.title: Scenes From A Pandemic Economy: 4 American Indicators
rows.standfirst: The pandemic economy has left different people in vastly different situations. Today, we introduce four American indicators — people whose paths will help us understand the arc of the recovery. Hear their stories now, and we'll follow up with them in a few months:

rows.title: U.S. 'Stands With The People,' Imposes Sanctions On Myanmar's Coup Leaders
rows.standfirst: The Treasury Department froze the assets of 10 current and retired top-ranking military leaders in Myanmar after a coup earlier this month that toppled the government of Aung San Suu Kyi.

rows.title: Federal Budget Deficit Expected To Hit Second Largest Since World War II
rows.standfirst: Congressional forecasters expect the federal deficit will hit the second largest in decades, even without factoring in President Biden's proposed $1.9 trillion coronavirus relief plan.

rows.title: Clubhouse May Be Social Media's Future. What's All The Hype About?
rows.standfirst: The invite-only app lets you eavesdrop on chats between celebrities, journalists and tech savants. Oprah, Elon Musk and White House Chief of Staff Ron Klain have all joined.

rows.title: Small Local Banks Make A Big Difference For Black-Owned Businesses Trying To Hang On
rows.standfirst: Black-owned businesses were often at the back of the line when the first coronavirus relief loans were doled out. Now, some are turning to banks that specialize in minority firms for help.

rows.title: 'They're Going To Eat Our Lunch,' Biden Warns After Call With China's Xi
rows.standfirst: After a two-hour phone call with his Chinese counterpart, President Biden made his case for domestic investment in infrastructure, clean energy and other sectors.

rows.title: Biden Administration Pauses Trump's TikTok Ban, Backs Off Pressure To Sell App
rows.standfirst: TikTok will still undergo a national security review by federal officials, but any outright ban, or pressure to sell to an American company, will not be a priority of the Biden White House.

rows.title: China-U.S. Trade Agreement Fail
rows.standfirst: Last year, China pledged to vastly increase its U.S. imports during 2020 and 2021. We ask economist Chad Bown if actual spending has been keeping pace with what was promised.

rows.title: After Days Of Mass Outages, Some Texas Residents Now Face Huge Electricity Bills
rows.standfirst: Texas allows companies to sell electricity at wholesale prices. When the price of electricity skyrocketed last week, that meant exorbitant bills for many residents who had been trying to save money.

rows.title: Natural Gas Companies Have Their Own Plans To Go Low-Carbon
rows.standfirst: The companies face an existential threat as more governments and businesses move to tackle climate change. So a growing number have their own plans to decarbonize, by creating renewable gas.

rows.title: Debris Falls From The Sky Near Denver After Flight Suffers Engine Failure
rows.standfirst: A Hawaii-bound United Airlines flight was forced to make an emergency landing at Denver's airport after experiencing an engine failure shortly after takeoff. There are no reports of injuries.

rows.title: Controls On Vaccine Exports 'Hold Back' Pandemic Recovery, Warns Incoming WTO Head
rows.standfirst: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is set to lead the World Trade Organization. She talked with NPR about the WTO's role in improving access to vaccines and says there's "no doubt" that the WTO needs reforms.

rows.title: American Indicators: The Faces And Stories Behind The Economic Statistics
rows.standfirst: Some sectors are thriving, while others continue to struggle, putting different people in vastly different situations. NPR is following four people who will help illustrate the arc of the recovery.

rows.title: FACT CHECK: Biden's Comments On Loan Forgiveness And Elite Colleges
rows.standfirst: The president said he doesn't want to forgive the loans of people who went to "Harvard and Yale and Penn." The real picture of student debt in the U.S. is much more complicated.

rows.title: A Bicycle. A Trip. Or Just Pants: The Things We Buy When Pining For Normal Times
rows.standfirst: Even the most mundane purchases are becoming objects of hope as we crave the routines and experiences of daily life in this period of isolation.

rows.title: We Buy A Superhero 2: Loophole
rows.standfirst: Marvel was not interested in selling us Doorman. But there is another way to jumpstart our superhero empire. | Find the full Planet Money Superhero series here.

rows.title: Cold Fronts, Propane And New Jobs - Indicators Of The Week
rows.standfirst: For our indicators of the week, we're talking about shortages of heating sources during the recent cold snap and trends amongst unemployed Americans.

rows.title: Bitcoin - The Religion
rows.standfirst: As the value of a bitcoin recently passed $50,000, market watchers struggled to explain how a virtual currency could reach such dizzy heights. One possible answer? It's kind of like a religion.

rows.title: Texas Is Defined By Energy. How Did The State's Power Grid Fail So Massively?
rows.standfirst: Millions of people in Texas have gone three or more days without power, water or both. Texas has had winter weather before, so what went so wrong this time?

rows.title: No, The Blackouts In Texas Weren't Caused By Renewables. Here's What Really Happened
rows.standfirst: Some prominent Republicans have blamed wind and solar power for the blackouts in the storm-stricken state. But the truth is that every source of generation fell short.

rows.title: Several Days Into The Texas Deep Freeze, Food Is Scarce
rows.standfirst: Amid power and water shutdowns, the extreme cold is disrupting the food supply. Customers are finding empty grocery shelves across Texas and people desperate to stock up are forming long lines.

rows.title: Almost A Year Into The Pandemic, Working Moms Feel 'Forgotten,' Journalist Says
rows.standfirst: Claire Cain Miller says many working moms have scaled back on their hours or left the workforce entirely in response to new household burdens. "There were never the structures in place to help us."

rows.title: Jerry Jones' Company Hits 'Jackpot' As Harsh Storms Send Natural Gas Prices Surging
rows.standfirst: A drilling company controlled by the Dallas Cowboys owner said it was benefitting after natural gas prices surged in the middle of powerful winter storms.

rows.title: Need A Career Change? Here's The Best Job Advice We've Heard On Life Kit
rows.standfirst: From quitting gracefully to asking for more money, here's how the experts advise navigating major career conundrums.

rows.title: The Power Is Back On In Texas. Now Comes The Recovery, And It Won't Be Cheap
rows.standfirst: From potential long-term rate hikes to repairs of broken pipes, Texans could be paying for years after the state's devastating blackouts.

rows.title: House Passes $1.9 Trillion COVID-19 Plan; Biden Calls For 'Quick Action' From Senate
rows.standfirst: The proposal, which would provide a new round of financial support for workers, families and businesses, will now advance to the Senate.

rows.title: We Buy A Superhero 3: Resurrection
rows.standfirst: We have found the perfect superhero. Now we just have to make him our own. | Find the full Planet Money Superhero series here.

rows.title: Unemployment Insurance And Vaccines: Who's Left Behind?
rows.standfirst: Two of the most important ways the government is supporting Americans right now is through distributing vaccines and providing unemployment insurance. But are there cracks in the system?

rows.title: Energy Secretary Granholm: Texas Outages Show Need For Changes To U.S. Power Systems
rows.standfirst: In her first interview with NPR since taking office, Jennifer Granholm made the case for sweeping reforms in order to meet President Biden's pledge to make the U.S. carbon neutral by 2050.

rows.title: British Airways Owner Calls For Digital Health Passes For Passengers
rows.standfirst: Luis Gallego, the CEO of International Airlines Group, wants "common testing standards and the introduction of digital health passes."

rows.title: Why Is Facebook Launching An All-Out War On Apple's Upcoming iPhone Update?
rows.standfirst: Facebook's Mark Zuckerberg and Apple's Tim Cook are fighting over iPhone privacy rules. At stake is the future of how iPhone user data is used by data brokers and advertisers.

rows.title: College Tuition Sparked A Mental Health Crisis. Then The Hefty Hospital Bill Arrived
rows.standfirst: A student sought counseling help after panicking over a tuition bill. A weeklong stay in a psychiatric hospital followed — along with a $3,413 bill. The hospital soft-pedaled its charity care policy.

rows.title: Biden's $1.9 Trillion Rescue Plan: Vital Medicine Or Costly Overkill?
rows.standfirst: Backers of the president's ambitious stimulus plan say it will help struggling families and businesses, but critics say it goes too far.

rows.title: TikTok To Pay $92 Million To Settle Class-Action Suit Over 'Theft' Of Personal Data
rows.standfirst: The proposed settlement applies to 89 million TikTok users in the U.S. whose personal data was allegedly tracked and sold to advertisers in violation of state and federal law.

rows.title: 2021: The Year Of The Recovery?
rows.standfirst: 2020 was a horrific year for the economy. We're hoping 2021 will be better, but will it? We discuss 3 indicators that suggest this year is shaping up to be better than last year.

rows.title: COVID-19 Vaccine Makers' Booster Shots Aim At A Moving Target: Coronavirus Variants
rows.standfirst: In the future, different circumstances will likely determine which vaccine or booster a person receives, based on their antibodies — and which variant is common in their region.

rows.title: Costco To Raise Minimum Wage To $16 An Hour: 'This Isn't Altruism'
rows.standfirst: Next week's pay increase would put Costco ahead of much of the industry. CEO W. Craig Jelinek said higher pay reduces turnover and boosts productivity.

rows.title: Watchdog Faults FAA For 'Significant Misunderstanding' Of Flight System
rows.standfirst: The inspector general for the Transportation Department says U.S. regulators must address oversight failures that led to two deadly Boeing 737 Max crashes in 2018 and 2019.
